recipes.name: Blue Cheese and Dried Cranberry Tossed Salad

steps.text: Layer romaine lettuce, grape tomatoes, cucumber, pecans, cranberries, and blue cheese in a large salad bowl. Toss salad with balsamic vinaigrette before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Blue Cheese and Dried Cranberry Tossed Salad
raw_recipe.description: This salad is a tried and true crowd pleaser. A basic romaine salad is dressed up with toasted pecans, cranberries, and crumbled blue cheese and tossed with balsamic vinaigrette to serve. Make this an easy meal by adding grilled chicken and serving with a crusty baguette.
raw_recipe.name: Blue Cheese and Dried Cranberry Tossed Salad

recipeInstructions.text: Layer romaine lettuce, grape tomatoes, cucumber, pecans, cranberries, and blue cheese in a large salad bowl. Toss salad with balsamic vinaigrette before serving.

review.reviewBody: I made this salad with a couple adjustments. I didn't have cuke, so I added some sliced red onion and also some apple chunks. It is now my absolute fave summer salad. Try adding blueberries, also, it's a great salad for fruit and the balsamic tastes great with it all!

This was so delicious it almost didn't need vinaigrette. I had no grape tomatoes so cut up small hothouse tomatoes instead. I also used the bulk spring salad greens as well as some romain hearts. Then I made a simple salad dressing of a very aged balsamic vinegar (which has an amazing sweet flavour) and a gourmet orange olive oil, salt and pepper and that made the salad perfect. I recommend you use a high quality vinaigrette or high quality ingredients to make your own. Be careful not to burn your pecans when you toast them in the cast iron pan!

Loved this fresh and classic salad! I took a few liberties on the ingredients such as cherub tomatoes vs grape tomatoes, used the regular cucumber in my fridge rather than English not in my fridge, and my favorite addition was to make a the balsamic vinaigrette from this Allrecipes recipe: https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/218337/our-favorite-balsamic-vinaigrette/ You could add almost any fresh vegetable and herb to this and it would still be a winner winner pre-dinner first course!

I've made this three times in the past two weeks, once with Romaine, once with iceberg blend and once with spinach. We liked the spinach best. Made w/o cukes and didn't miss 'em a bit. This is definitely a keeper!

I made this for our family Christmas dinner. The only thing that I omitted was the cucumber - I didn't see how that would enhance the flavor of the salad with the blue cheese and toasted pecans. I used Paul Newman's Light Cranberry Walnut dressing. I think next time I would use a balsamic vinaigrette instead and add a little purple/red onion for a little more kick. Will definately make a again as it was a beautiful salad for the holiday! Thanks for the recipe!
I added a little raspberry vinaigrette to the dressing and "snowed" the frozen blue cheese over the top.

This is an amazing salad! I personally don't add the cucumbers and walnuts. The combination of tomato, blue cheese, and cranberry works so well together, sometimes i just skip the lettuce and eat that by itself! I use oil and red wine vinegar as my dressing and the flavor is perfect.

Instead of the cucumber and tomatoes - add a Granny Smith apple or a large Anju Pear - you don't have to toast the nuts - just put a handful of walnuts - cracked pepper - salt and a good Olive Oil. I love using Iceberg instead of Romaine lettuce.

I took this to a church luncheon. It was SO easy to put together, but looked very festive in a trifle dish. I didn't dress it, just put a bottle of fat free raspberry vinaigrette next to the bowl. All gone!

Very good. Served it at a family dinner and many were going back for 2nd and 3rd helpings. I would make sure to add the balsamic vinaigrette just before serving because after a while the salad started to wilt. Or you could have it on the side and let people add it themselves.

I made this recipe exactly as written, with no changes or substitutions, except I reduced the amount of blue cheese by 50 percent, because it was over-powering. While all the ingredients sounded wonderful together, this salad could have been saved using a different dressing. Just using balsamic vinegar alone as the sole dressing on this salad ruined it - it did not go with the salad at all. Only two out of 7 people liked the salad, but I think they were being polite. With a different dressing, this salad could have been saved. Good ingredients; with an expensive salad, I would highly recommend a different dressing.
Substitute the cranberries for dried cherries & use cherry vinaigrette (can be hard to find)....candied walnuts & red onions. Once you have had it, you won’t go back!
Don't change a thing!
I tweaked it slightly adding some spinach, red onion, and celery. I wouldn't change a think except for dressing the salad with variations of vinaigrette's. It was a very good salad.
Very good salad! Will use it again.
Great combo of flavors...you must toast nuts, given the option. Makes a big difference when you do.
This salad was awesome! It almost tasted like the chopped salad at Outback Steakhouse. Next time I will chop up the Romano lettuce a little more. This made for a great and quick dinner!

Fabulous salad, very filling. My only caveat is to go light on the walnuts, since too many nuts can leave an aftertaste and take away from the great flavors in this salad. That's just my own taste, though. Overall, this is a delicious salad.
Love it! Would be great as a main meal with grilled chicken breast added. Next time I might add some red/orange/yellow pepper slices.
Very good salad made by my wife. Recommended.
